investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-22T09:52–09:59Z because every agent pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained stuck for 135–146 seconds before the eval timeout was reached and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving remote agent pods (production-api environment) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that no node in the 6-node cluster could accept a new remote agent pod at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") never received a vmId or remoteState, causing all four required evidence fields to remain missing and all contract assertions to fail. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this eval run.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have claimed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely] Node affinity or node selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, meaning the 4 remaining nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger pool, shrinking available capacity without a corresponding reduction in demand.
[Possible] A resource leak or stuck pod from a prior eval run or user workload is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new pods from scheduling.

[Lower likelihood] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource advertised capacity on the 2 eligible nodes was reduced by a node configuration change, DaemonSet update, or peer-pod provider quota change.

No agent was ever provisioned, so the runner never reached the state-polling step and produced zero evidence, violating the expected-output contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage, though the same scheduling bottleneck would affect real remote agent provisioning requests if the cluster is at capacity.

investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness attempted to exercise model aura-gpt-5-5 via POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test and received a 502 response whose body contains an Anthropic API 429 rate_limit_error with the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider." The harness classified this as error code bad_gateway and marked the model result ok=false with provider=null and resolvedModel=null. Because one model failed, the probe set allPassed=false and failedModelCount=1, violating the expected-output contract assertions defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json at line 333 (allPassed equals true) and line 334 (failedModelCount equals 0). The failure is localized to the aura-gpt-5-5 model slot; the sibling model aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 passed cleanly.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-22T09:52–09:59Z because every agent pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=536 exceeds max 300)
investigations.summary: The eval check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the observability snapshot published at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 536 minutes old, which exceeds the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. This is an eval-layer staleness failure localized to the snapshot publication pipeline; all sibling public-website checks (public-observability-page, public-models-page, public-marketing-pages) passed, confirming the web surfaces themselves are reachable.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. At eval time (2026-07-22T09:59:41Z), the snapshot was 536 minutes old — approximately 8 hours and 56 minutes since last publication — meaning the workflow was either skipped, failed silently, or was blocked for roughly the last 4+ hours beyond the allowed staleness threshold. The eval contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) asserts snapshotAgeMinutes max 300; the live evidence value of 536 directly violates this assertion.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 536' — the sole violated assertion, confirmed by the check message and raw evidence.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=536, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and was previously generated by GitHub Actions but is now stale.
expected-output.contract: infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 asserts { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } — the contract boundary that was crossed.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: registry config shows staleAfterMinutes=360 for this check, which is looser than the contract's max 300 — a secondary tension worth noting but not the direct cause of this failure.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed with HTTP 200 — confirms the public website is reachable and the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness, not site availability.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload — the probe itself executed successfully (latencyMs=151), meaning the staleness value is real data from the live URL, not a fetch error.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot to https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json failed, was cancelled, or was skipped during the ~9-hour window before this eval ran, leaving the previously published stale file in place.

Second: The scheduled trigger for the snapshot-publishing GitHub Actions workflow was disabled, misconfigured, or missed its schedule window (e.g., due to GitHub Actions queue delays or a repository-level workflow pause).

Third: The workflow ran but failed at the publish/deploy step (e.g., GitHub Pages deployment error, permissions issue, or branch protection rule), so the snapshot file on GitHub Pages was not updated even though the workflow was triggered.

Fourth: A configuration tension exists between the registry's staleAfterMinutes=360 (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) and the contract's maxAgeMinutes=300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482/486). If the workflow runs on a cadence aligned to 360 minutes rather than 300, the snapshot could routinely exceed the contract threshold even when the workflow is healthy. At 536 minutes, however, this alone does not explain the current failure — the workflow appears to have missed at least one full cycle.
